The block parity and signed cut arguments are correctFor a closed block  $X$ , the covered domain of  $N|_X$  has size
$$2|A_X|+a_X+b_X+2t_X.$$
Because  $N|_X$  is a matching covering that domain, this number is even. Therefore
$$a_X+b_X\equiv 0\pmod 2.$$
Neither arbitrary rematching of the old PP vertices nor activation of whole mixed pairs changes this conclusion. The latter contributes exactly two covered vertices per activated pair.The stronger signed identity also has the correct signs and factors. The old  $A$ -covered vertices have total sign zero. Activated mixed pairs contribute one negative and one positive selected endpoint. Consequently, the sign sum on the covered domain inside  $X$  is
$$b_X-a_X.$$
Computing the same sum through the matching edges gives
$$b_X-a_X=2h_{+,X}-2h_{-,X},$$
which is precisely
$$a_X-b_X=2(h_{-,X}-h_{+,X}).$$
Thus
$$h_{-,X}\ge \frac12\max(a_X-b_X,0).$$
The blocks are disjoint and no matching edge leaves a closed block, so summing these lower bounds does not charge an error edge twice. Since the global source and resource totals agree,
$$\sum_X(a_X-b_X)=0,$$

\frac12\sum_X\max(a_X-b_X,0)
=
\frac14\sum_X|a_X-b_X|.$$

\le |N\text{ crossing }X|
\le \nu(E\text{ crossing }X).$$
